turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would call Estella at once, and he moved towards the door with a mixture of nervousness and curiosity.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip move towards the door with a keen eye, her expression unreadable. She told Pip to wait a moment and instructed him to fetch Estella from her chambers, ensuring he knew the way.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would fetch Estella right away and asked for directions to her chambers.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham instructed Pip to take a left at the grand staircase and proceed down the corridor until he reached a set of smaller doors, which would be Estella’s chambers. She watched him carefully, noting his hesitance and curiosity, and felt a strange mix of amusement and detachment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip thanked Miss Havisham for the directions and proceeded towards the grand staircase with a tentative step, his heart beating a little faster as he wondered what Estella would be like.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip ascend the grand staircase with a mixture of detachment and a strange, cold interest, her eyes lingering on his retreating form as if she were studying a specimen.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt his palms grow damp as he reached the top of the grand staircase and turned left towards the corridor Miss Havisham had described, his mind racing with questions about Estella and why Miss Havisham wanted him to fetch her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip's departure with a keen eye, her thoughts swirling with the complexities of her past and the enigma that was Estella. She felt a peculiar sense of satisfaction in orchestrating this encounter between Pip and her protégée, though the reasons behind it remained shrouded in her own labyrinthine mind.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip knocked gently on the smaller doors at the end of the corridor, his heart pounding as he waited for an answer.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched as Pip knocked on the door at the end of the corridor, her eyes narrowing as if she were observing a chess move in a game she alone understood.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip asked softly through the door, his voice barely more than a whisper, if Estella was there and if she would come out to see him.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the door, her eyes glinting with an enigmatic light as she waited for Estella to appear. She told herself that this was a test, a way to see how Pip would fare under the scrutiny of her protégée.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip asked Miss Havisham if she had any instructions for him while he was there, his voice small and filled with a mixture of curiosity and trepidation.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she had few instructions, her tone both dismissive and enigmatic, as if the boy's expectations would be shaped more by the atmosphere of her home than by any direct guidance.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he understood and would do his best to please her, though he felt a bit uncertain about what exactly was expected of him.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham observed Pip with a mixture of disdain and curiosity, her eyes narrowing as she took in the young boy’s uncertain demeanor. She told him that he was to amuse her, but how he chose to do so was entirely up to him, a challenge wrapped in a thinly veiled insult.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would do his best to find a way to amuse her, though his heart was heavy with uncertainty about how to proceed.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she would be watching his efforts closely, her words laden with a promise of critique that left the boy feeling even more anxious and unsure of himself.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would try his very best, though the task seemed daunting and he was unsure how to proceed without offending her further.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that he should not trouble himself, for she had no intention of making his visit a pleasant one, and if he found her company unbearable, he was welcome to leave.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
